title: When to Intervene? An Empirical Study of Errors and Self-Recovery in LLM Agents
why: Analyzes natural self-recovery and predicts when external intervention is necessary.

title: CUA-Recovery: Benchmarking Error Recovery in Long-Horizon Computer-Use Agents
why: Benchmarks recognition and repair of inherited desktop errors over persistent workflows.

title: Back Up Before You Regret: Measuring Backup Awareness and Automating Backup in Coding Agents
why: Studies preventive backup and the BackUpper layer for coding agent actions.
note: Does not imply external effects are reversible.

title: Sentry: Learning to Recover from LLM Agent Failures at Test Time
why: Conditionally retrieves failure lessons and verifies repaired execution.

title: AgentDebugX: An Open-Source Toolkit for Failure Observability, Attribution, and Recovery in LLM Agents
why: Links evidence-grounded failure diagnosis to bounded recovery proposals and controlled reruns.
note: EMNLP 2026 System Demonstrations; GAIA rerun results are author-reported and need a controlled environment.

title: AgentRx: Diagnosing AI Agent Failures from Execution Trajectories
why: Synthesizes per-step constraints and auditable violation logs to localize critical failure steps.
note: EMNLP 2026 Findings; 170 annotated trajectories in final ACL version (earlier Microsoft materials mention 115); diagnosis only.

title: CUADebug: Diagnosing and Repairing Computer-Use Agent Failures
why: Inspects paired screenshots and actions for causal GUI errors and conditions re-execution on structured diagnosis.
note: EMNLP 2026 Findings; CUAErrorBench has 204 annotated failures; rerollout results depend on controlled restart settings.

title: TRAJDEBUG: Tracing Error Lifecycle to Identify Critical Failures in Long-Horizon Agent Trajectories
why: Separates initially wrong decisions from resolved errors and terminally relevant causal failures in long traces.
note: EMNLP 2026 Findings; TrajErrBench reports 486 annotated failed trajectories; step localization is not rollback.

title: Agent Error Dataset: Scaling 50,000 Error--Diagnosis Pairs for Failure Analysis and Error-Aware Post-Training
why: Pairs error diagnoses with candidate corrections and matched replay from common checkpoints when available.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint; 50228 pairs and 3062 matched reruns are author-reported; resettable environments only.

title: Locating Hidden Failures Makes Long-Horizon Agents More Reliable
why: Traverse labels mistakes and Scout predicts first-error locations.

title: MeshHeal: Two-Timescale Self-Healing for Gray Failures in Decentralized LLM Agent Networks
why: Explores escalation and verification during containment and reintegration of degraded agents.

title: Self-Healing Harness for Runtime Oversight of Agent Self-Modification
why: Gates persistent agent self-modifications on demonstrated improvement without unacceptable regressions.

title: Collective Loss of Control in LLM Agent Systems: An Epidemic Account of Mutation, Contagion, and Recovery
why: Analyzes how erroneous agent behaviors spread across multi-agent systems and recover.

title: Agent Error Simulator: Fault Injection for Testing Recovery in Agentic Workflows
why: Declarative proxy fault injection probes format logic and tool failures across planner worker and aggregator roles.
note: IEEE eScience 2026; results from an example hierarchical workflow and HPC-centric setup, not broad agent robustness.

title: Localizing Emergent Failures in Agentic AI: Recovering Minimal Repair Families via Counterfactual Replay
why: Uses graph-constrained counterfactual replay to test combined repair interventions.

title: AgentRewind: Recoverable Execution for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
why: Aligns agent-context and environment-state checkpoints for resumable execution.

title: When Agentic Executions Fail: Detecting and Localizing Runtime Faults from Telemetry
why: AgentChaosBench injects MCP A2A guardrail and tool faults and evaluates fault localization from aligned execution traces.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint; 275 traces (250 faulty and 25 control); measures diagnosis, not verified task recovery.

title: Real-Time Detection and Repair of LLM Agent Failures
why: Combines step telemetry and deterministic verification with repair experiments.

title: Speculative Rollback Correction for Quality-Diverse Web Agent Imitation
why: Uses branch-level rollback and correction for resettable training-time web agents.

title: When Tools Fail: Benchmarking Dynamic Replanning and Anomaly Recovery in LLM Agents
why: ToolMaze tests explicit or implicit transient or permanent tool perturbations.

title: Debugging the Debuggers: Failure-Anchored Structured Recovery for Software Engineering Agents
why: PROBE gates recovery guidance on structured telemetry and grounded diagnosis for subsequent repair attempts.
note: ASE 2026 paper; 257 initially unresolved cases and outcomes reported by authors; diagnosis does not itself guarantee recovery.

title: Crab: A Semantics-Aware Checkpoint/Restore Runtime for Agent Sandboxes
why: Uses OS-effect inspection to make agent sandbox checkpointing more selective.

title: ReliabilityBench: Evaluating LLM Agent Reliability Under Production-Like Stress Conditions
why: Studies robustness and repeated agent reliability under controlled stress.

title: DoVer: Intervention-Driven Auto Debugging for LLM Multi-Agent Systems
why: Verifies debugging hypotheses by actively intervening in multi-agent tasks.

title: A Survey for LLM Agent Trajectory Analysis: From Failure Attribution to Enhancement
why: Surveys agent trajectory attribution and the connections to agent enhancement.

title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
why: Feedback-based learning across attempts informs recovery design.

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
why: Foundational combined reasoning and acting tool-use loop.
